To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sorption-desorption behavior is highly dependent on the type of pesticide and soil, but it can be predicted through principal component analysis.

the sorption of pesticides and their metabolites in volcanic and non-volcanic soils can be related to organic matter content, pH and clay minerals, but the contribution of aluminum oxides and crystalline minerals is also important.
the high sorption of acidic compounds in volcanic soils was mainly related to the presence of amorphous oxides of Al in Andisols, and to the presence of crystalline minerals in Ultisols.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a global interpretation of the sorption behavior of pesticides and some of their degradation products on different types of soils.
the sorption behavior of pesticides and degradation products in volcanic soils.
the sorption of six pesticides and their degradation compounds on seven soils belonging to four soil orders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sorption behavior of pesticides and metabolites is strongly dependent on the chemical nature of the soil, which is a function of the soil order.

the sorption of pesticides in Andisol and Ultisol soils is controlled by the content of amorphous Al-oxide and crystalline minerals, respectively, and the retention in Mollisol and Alfisol soils is controlled mainly by organic matter content.
sorption of acidic pesticides and their metabolites was strongly influenced by mineral contents, whereas sorption of neutral compounds was mainly related to organic matter content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acidic pesticides are not retained in volcanic soils, but they are in nonvolcanic ones, whereas basic pesticides are retained on all soils.
the sorption of acidic pesticides is mainly governed by mineral surfaces in volcanic soils, while in nonvolcanic ones it would depend on organic carbon content.

acidic compounds were weakly sorbed in Mollisools and Alfisols and could be leached in Andisols or Ultisols, whereas atrazine and its degradation product were weakly retained in Mollisolls and Alfisols but strongly in Andisols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sorption-desorption behavior and fate of pesticides in volcanic soils is different from that in nonvolcanic soil orders.
the interpretation of pesticide sorption data by PCA is a powerful tool that can be used in a wide range of situations.
the sorption-desorption behavior and the mobility of the pesticides and their degradation compounds are strongly influenced by the mineralogy of the soils.
